mission: Least-privilege Postgres role separation for the consent system: MIGRATION_OWNER / APPLICATION_RUNTIME / WORKER_RUNTIME / READONLY, with SQL grants via the repo migration system, docker-compose bootstrap wiring, and service connection-role separation.
method: New migration 0018_consent_role_separation.sql creates four cluster-wide NOLOGIN group roles (idempotent, race-safe across the per-suite-schema test pattern) and applies per-schema grants: full DML on ordinary tables for the two runtime roles, SELECT-only for readonly, plus consent carve-outs (consent_record: no UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE; consent_subject: no DELETE; consent_subject_erasure and schema_migrations: read-only) and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for future migrations. Runtime roles own nothing, so ALTER/DROP/trigger-disable on the consent schema are denied by ownership. consent_subject deletion happens only via the app_user FK cascade, which executes with owner privileges, so the worker keeps zero direct delete rights on consent tables while account deletion still tombstones correctly. infra/postgres/init-roles.sql (mounted as /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d in both compose Postgres containers) creates local login users pickle_app/pickle_worker/pickle_ro/pickle_migrator holding membership in the group roles. services/api reads DATABASE_URL_APP and services/media-worker reads DATABASE_URL_WORKER, both falling back to DATABASE_URL for back-compat; migrations/seed keep using owner DATABASE_URL. New integration suite packages/database/test/roles.integration.test.ts verifies the boundaries with SET ROLE against real Postgres.
datasetScopeAndGrouping: No ML dataset involved. Scope is the Postgres schema (migrations 0001-0018) exercised against local docker Postgres 16 (postgres_test, fresh volume with the init script). Verification grouped as: (a) new roles integration suite, (b) full existing root test suite including all consent integration/red-team/abuse/e2e suites, (c) a manual probe over a real pickle_app login connection (not just SET ROLE).
holdoutStatement: Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were not read, listed, referenced, or touched. This workstream is database/infrastructure only and used no video bundles or annotation data.

configuration.postgres: postgres:16-alpine via docker compose (postgres_test on :5433, fresh volume so init-roles.sql ran)

rolesIntegrationSuite.notes: Asserts per runtime role: append+read allowed on consent_record; UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE consent_record denied; DELETE consent_subject denied; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE consent_subject_erasure denied; INSERT/DELETE schema_migrations denied; ALTER TABLE / DISABLE TRIGGER / DROP TABLE / DROP TRIGGER / CREATE TABLE denied; worker DELETE app_user cascades and tombstones (1 tombstone row observed); readonly SELECT-only; default privileges cover a table created after 0018.

rootGates.test: pass: 593 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (DATABASE_URL_TEST set, all consent integration suites executed against real Postgres)

measuredResults.mobileGates: not affected by this change (no apps/mobile files touched); run anyway: npm ci OK, tsc --noEmit 0 errors, jest 397 passed / 397 total
measuredResults.realLoginProbe: Fresh schema migrated with owner creds (18 applied); connected as pickle_app login user: INSERT app_user OK, consent_subject ON CONFLICT upsert OK, consent_record append OK (seq 1), UPDATE consent_record -> ERROR: permission denied for table consent_record.

findings: The consent_subject ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE upsert used by services/api requires UPDATE privilege on consent_subject; the 0017 immutability trigger still rejects any real change, so granting UPDATE preserves the intended no-rewrite property while keeping the existing query shape working.

FK ON DELETE CASCADE executes with the referencing table owner's privileges, so the worker needs only DELETE on app_user for account deletion; the consent_subject tombstone trigger fires under owner privileges and the worker holds no INSERT on consent_subject_erasure.

Roles are cluster-wide but the test pattern migrates many throwaway schemas concurrently, so role creation must be race-safe (duplicate_object caught) and grants must be re-applied per schema; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is scoped per schema and is dropped with DROP SCHEMA CASCADE, so test cleanup is unaffected.

Privilege-level enforcement is defense in depth on top of the 0015/0016/0017 triggers: even a runtime credential compromise cannot disable those triggers (ownership required) or bulk-erase the ledger (no TRUNCATE granted).
Back-compat verified: the full pre-existing suite (593 tests) passes unchanged with superuser DATABASE_URL_TEST, i.e. single-credential local setups are unaffected.
verdictRationale: All privilege boundaries are implemented, migrated through the repo's migration system, and verified with counts against real local Postgres 16 (7/7 new role tests incl. 22 denied-operation assertions; 593/593 existing tests pass; real pickle_app login connection confirmed allowed/denied paths). PROVISIONAL rather than GREEN because production credential provisioning (AWS Secrets Manager values, RDS role ownership transfer to pickle_migration_owner) is external to this repo and unexercised here, and existing local dev volumes only pick up the login users after volume recreation or a manual psql apply.
